items.title: Could Your Android TV Box Run AI Malware?
items.summary: A cheap Android TV box with its debug port deliberately left open was all an Anthropic lab test needed to show AI malware copying itself to another device on the same network. It was slow, the small models struggled to chain actions, and nothing like it has been reported in the wild. So where is the real risk? In this episode of Debug Mode, the hosts trade takes on the claim that being rude to Anthropic’s model can cost you access: is an angry session abuse, or the agent-era rage click? Then one host’s rabbit hole: malware that rewrites its own fingerprint, taps a local model already on your machine, or slips in through an MCP tool that changes after install. You’ll hear why allow-listing tools at connect time matters, why blocking outbound traffic can starve remote-inference malware, and why the person choosing what to install is still the weak link. One host went looking for an antivirus that catches malware using local models and couldn’t find any. Have you? Tell us below, and subscribe for the next episode.
